findings: Missing generator, truncated generator, corrupted header, and decoder-passed-as-generator each fail in under 0.25 s with exit code 1 and a clear message; the truncated case names the tensor and recommends re-downloading
A missing decoder is only detected after about 13 s of generation, because the decoder loads last: the worker must check every required file before launch

Same-size corruption inside the decoder's tensor data exits 0 and writes a complete, finite, entirely silent WAV (peak 0.0): the engine does not detect corrupt weights, so MOD-005/006 hash verification is essential and the app should also reject silent output

With a helper holding VRAM so that only 3.3 GB or 6.4 GB was free (below the ~5.6 GB peak for the first), generation still succeeded, taking 15.8 s of pipeline time vs 14.0 s. Under WDDM the driver can page idle allocations and fall back to system memory, so scarce VRAM appeared as a slowdown, not an error
A genuine CUDA out-of-memory failure was not reproduced here; it needs a GPU with less VRAM or an actively competing workload
